needs.text: The Amazon EFS CSI driver add-on with its Pod Identity role, and an EFS file system with a mount target in each cluster subnet. Put the file system’s ID in fileSystemId.

blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: The first object is a StorageClass for Amazon EFS. It comes from storage.k8s.io/v1.
blocks.why: EFS is a shared file system. Many Pods on many nodes can use it at once.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: A recipe for shared storage on Amazon EFS

blocks.title: Who makes the storage?
blocks.what: efs uses the Amazon EFS CSI driver, efs.csi.aws.com.
blocks.why: Auto Mode includes EBS but not EFS, so you install this driver as an add-on.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the StorageClass, because it needs a provisioner.
blocks.comment: The EFS CSI driver makes the storage
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: efs
provisioner: efs.csi.aws.com

blocks.title: Which file system?
blocks.what: efs-ap gives each claim its own access point: a private directory. fileSystemId is a placeholder for yours.
blocks.why: aws efs describe-file-systems lists your IDs. directoryPerms: "700" lets only the owner use the directory.
blocks.ifRemoved: The driver cannot tell which file system to use, so claims stay Pending.
blocks.comment: A directory of its own in your EFS file system for each claim
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: efs
provisioner: efs.csi.aws.com
parameters:
  provisioningMode: efs-ap
  fileSystemId: fs-0123456789abcdef0
  directoryPerms: "700"

blocks.title: Ask for shared storage
blocks.what: Three dashes start a second object: a PersistentVolumeClaim called shared.
blocks.why: Pods use storage through a claim.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A second object: a request for shared storage
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: efs
provisioner: efs.csi.aws.com
parameters:
  provisioningMode: efs-ap
  fileSystemId: fs-0123456789abcdef0
  directoryPerms: "700"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: shared

blocks.title: Shared by many
blocks.what: The claim uses the efs StorageClass. ReadWriteMany lets Pods on many nodes read and write at once.
blocks.why: EBS allows one node at a time. EFS allows many, which this lesson needs.
blocks.ifRemoved: The cluster’s default StorageClass is used, which may not share at all.
blocks.comment: EFS, usable by Pods on many nodes at once
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: efs
provisioner: efs.csi.aws.com
parameters:
  provisioningMode: efs-ap
  fileSystemId: fs-0123456789abcdef0
  directoryPerms: "700"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: shared
spec:
  storageClassName: efs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany

blocks.title: How big?
blocks.why: Kubernetes requires a size. EFS grows as you write, and charges for what you store.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the claim, because it must say how much storage it needs.
blocks.comment: A size, which EFS requires but does not enforce
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: efs
provisioner: efs.csi.aws.com
parameters:
  provisioningMode: efs-ap
  fileSystemId: fs-0123456789abcdef0
  directoryPerms: "700"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: shared
spec:
  storageClassName: efs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi

blocks.title: Pods to share it
blocks.what: Three dashes start a third object: a Deployment called writers.
blocks.why: Two Pods will write to the same file.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A third object: two Pods that share the storage
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: efs
provisioner: efs.csi.aws.com
parameters:
  provisioningMode: efs-ap
  fileSystemId: fs-0123456789abcdef0
  directoryPerms: "700"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: shared
spec:
  storageClassName: efs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: writers

blocks.title: Two copies
blocks.what: Keep two Pods, labelled app: writers.
blocks.why: Two Pods show that both see the same file.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because apps/v1 Deployments must have a selector.
blocks.comment: Two copies of the Pods with this label
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: efs
provisioner: efs.csi.aws.com
parameters:
  provisioningMode: efs-ap
  fileSystemId: fs-0123456789abcdef0
  directoryPerms: "700"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: shared
spec:
  storageClassName: efs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: writers
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: writers

blocks.title: Describe the Pods
blocks.what: The template gives each Pod the label app: writers.
blocks.why: The labels must match the selector.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Deployment would have nothing to create, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: efs
provisioner: efs.csi.aws.com
parameters:
  provisioningMode: efs-ap
  fileSystemId: fs-0123456789abcdef0
  directoryPerms: "700"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: shared
spec:
  storageClassName: efs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: writers
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: writers
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: writers

blocks.title: Sign the visitors’ book
blocks.what: Each Pod adds its own name to /shared/visitors, then sleeps.
blocks.why: Reading the file shows a line from every Pod.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Deployment, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: efs
provisioner: efs.csi.aws.com
parameters:
  provisioningMode: efs-ap
  fileSystemId: fs-0123456789abcdef0
  directoryPerms: "700"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: shared
spec:
  storageClassName: efs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: writers
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: writers
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: writers
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: writer
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo $(hostname) was here >> /shared/visitors && sleep 3600"]

blocks.title: Where the storage appears
blocks.what: The volume named shared appears at /shared.
blocks.why: Both Pods mount the same directory.
blocks.ifRemoved: Each Pod writes to its own storage, so the file holds one line.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: efs
provisioner: efs.csi.aws.com
parameters:
  provisioningMode: efs-ap
  fileSystemId: fs-0123456789abcdef0
  directoryPerms: "700"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: shared
spec:
  storageClassName: efs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: writers
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: writers
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: writers
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: writer
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo $(hostname) was here >> /shared/visitors && sleep 3600"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: shared
              mountPath: /shared

blocks.title: Which claim?
blocks.what: The volume named shared comes from the shared claim. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.why: Every Pod using the claim sees the same files.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Deployment, because the mount names a volume that does not exist.
blocks.comment: The volume is the shared claim
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: efs
provisioner: efs.csi.aws.com
parameters:
  provisioningMode: efs-ap
  fileSystemId: fs-0123456789abcdef0
  directoryPerms: "700"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: shared
spec:
  storageClassName: efs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: writers
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: writers
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: writers
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: writer
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo $(hostname) was here >> /shared/visitors && sleep 3600"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: shared
              mountPath: /shared
      volumes:
        - name: shared
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: shared

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version: storage.k8s.io/v1, core v1, and apps/v1.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.---: Three dashes separate objects. One file can hold several objects.
notes.StorageClass:kind: A recipe for making storage on demand.
notes.PersistentVolumeClaim:kind: A request for storage, which a StorageClass fulfils.
notes.Deployment:kind: A Deployment keeps identical Pods running.
notes.StorageClass:metadata.name: The recipe’s name. Claims choose it with storageClassName.
notes.PersistentVolumeClaim:metadata.name: The claim’s name. The Deployment’s Pods refer to it.
notes.Deployment:metadata.name: The Deployment’s name. Its Pods’ names start with it.
notes.provisioner: efs.csi.aws.com: the Amazon EFS CSI driver, installed as an EKS add-on.
notes.parameters: EFS settings for each claim. Values are text.
notes.parameters.provisioningMode: efs-ap: make an EFS access point, a private directory, for each claim.
notes.parameters.fileSystemId: A placeholder. Replace it with your file system’s ID, from aws efs describe-file-systems.
notes.parameters.directoryPerms: Permissions for each new directory. "700": only its owner. Quotes keep it text.
notes.Deployment:spec: The desired state of the Deployment.
notes.spec.storageClassName: Which StorageClass makes the storage: efs.
notes.spec.accessModes: How the storage can be used.
notes.spec.accessModes[]: ReadWriteMany: Pods on many nodes can read and write at once.
notes.spec.resources: How much storage the claim needs.
notes.spec.resources.requests.storage: 5Gi. Kubernetes requires a size, but EFS does not limit it.
notes.spec.replicas: How many Pods to keep running: two.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for every Pod.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels: Labels given to every Pod. They must match the selector.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels.app: Every Pod gets the label app: writers.
notes.spec.template.spec: What each Pod runs, and which volumes it uses.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].command: Add this Pod’s name to /shared/visitors, then sleep.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].volumeMo: Where volumes appear inside the container.
Which volume: shared, defined under volumes.
notes.spec.template.spec.volumes[].name: The volume’s name, used by volumeMounts.
notes.spec.template.spec.volumes[].persistentV: The volume comes from a claim.

tryIt.result: Creates the StorageClass, the claim, and the Deployment. Replace the fileSystemId placeholder first.
STATUS turns Bound within seconds: the driver has made an access point.
Both Pods are Running. They may be on different nodes.
Prints two lines, one from each Pod. They share one file.
Removes all three and the access point. Delete the EFS file system yourself when you finish.

questions.question: Why does the claim use ReadWriteMany?
answers: So Pods on different nodes can use it at once
questions.explain: Both Pods write to the same storage, possibly from different nodes.

questions.question: What does provisioningMode: efs-ap make for each claim?
answers: An access point: a private directory in your file system
questions.explain: The file system already exists. Each claim gets its own directory in it.

questions.question: What must you change before applying?
answers: fileSystemId, to your own file system’s ID
questions.explain: fs-0123456789abcdef0 is a placeholder. aws efs describe-file-systems lists your real IDs.

fix.message: StorageClass in version "v1" cannot be handled as a StorageClass: json: cannot unmarshal number into Go struct field StorageClass.parameters of type string
fix.explain: StorageClass parameters must be text. Without quotes, YAML reads 700 as a number.
fix.fix: Put the value in quotes: directoryPerms: "700".
